title: Pulse Propagation
description: Simulate flip-flop and conjunction modules processing pulse signals.
writeup:
## Approach

The module network has three types: the broadcaster fans out to all targets, flip-flops toggle state on low pulses (ignoring high), and conjunction modules remember each input's last pulse and output low only when all inputs were last high.

## Part 1

Simulate 1000 button presses, processing pulses in FIFO order. Count total low and high pulses sent, then multiply the counts.

## Part 2

Determining when `rx` first receives a low pulse by simulation alone would take billions of presses. Inspecting the module graph reveals that `rx`'s sole input is a conjunction fed by several independent subnetworks. Each subnetwork cycles with its own period, sending a high pulse to the final conjunction once per cycle. The answer is the LCM of these cycle lengths — the first moment all subnetworks fire high simultaneously.
